title: Canonical hourly session delta layer for nearline Console analytics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a compact, canonical hourly delta layer that consolidates Console invocation events into deduplicated tenant-session records optimized for nearline queries (1–15 minute freshness). This layer is intended to power the Console UX heatmaps, per-route SLA dashboards, and realtime cost attribution slices without scanning wide event tables. Key features: stable canonical keys, deterministic session stitching, compact TTL compaction, and CDC-driven incremental updates.
updates: 2026-02-18: Ticket created after analytics working group identified slow dashboards backing on raw event scans.

2026-02-22: Data contract draft posted to Confluence; requested fields: tenant_id, route_id, session_id, session_start_ts, session_end_ts, invocation_count, token_count, coldstart_count, canonical_fingerprint.

2026-02-28: Spike complete — tested CDC throughput using Debezium stream; average applied rate 4k events/sec for a single shard. Chosen compaction strategy: hourly tombstone + upsert via Iceberg MERGE.
2026-03-03: Design review with PM & Console backend. Action: add alternate identity mapping table to handle workspace migrations and cross-workspace user unlinks.
2026-03-09: PR opened (github.com/redwood/warehouse/pull/2147). Feedback: need histogram bucketization for latency distribution and a compact route fingerprint to enable fast joins.

2026-03-12: Addressed PR comments; added unit tests for dedup window logic and end-to-end integration test against local Iceberg instance. Next: schedule canary backfill and monitor slot consumption in staging.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Hourly delta table (console_session_hourly) exists in curated warehouse with documented schema and column-level descriptions in Confluence.
A2: Ingestion pipeline applies CDC events and upserts within 5 minutes of arrival for >90% of events in staging under production-like load (4k events/sec shard).
A3: Session stitching deduplicates overlapping invocations with correct start/end heuristics (tests cover 1s, 5m, 30m gap cases).
A4: Query patterns for Console dashboards execute against the new table with median query time <= 400ms for typical filters (tenant + route + hour) and cost <50% of previous raw-event scans.
A5: Backfill completes for 30 days of historical data within maintenance window (estimated 6 hours) and produces identical aggregates to canonical ad-hoc job within 1% tolerance.
A6: Migration playbook documented and runbook added to PagerDuty rotation for any schema-change failures.
implementation_steps: 1) Finalize schema and publish data contract in Confluence (owner: Marcus).
2) Implement CDC consumer job that materializes incremental upserts into a staging iceberg table using small-file batching (owner: infra-analytics).
3) Implement deterministic canonical key generation (tenant_id + route_hash + session_window_hash) and fingerprinting library in warehouse codebase.
4) Add hourly compaction job: MERGE small staging files into console_session_hourly with TTL tombstones for sessions older than 90 days (owner: infra-analytics).
5) Add pre-aggregated latency histogram columns (p50,p90,p99) computed during compaction to avoid heavy aggregations in dashboard queries.
6) Create SQL views for Console dashboards that expose the minimal projection (tenant, route, hour, invocations, tokens, latency_buckets).
7) Add monitoring: ingestion lag metric, upsert error rate, compaction run duration, and query latency dashboards.
8) Run staged canary backfill for 7 days and validate aggregates vs existing ad-hoc aggregates, then proceed to 30-day backfill.
migration_plan: Run canary backfill against a single non-prod workspace replica. After validation, run incremental backfill in parallel lanes: partition by hour and run 12 parallel jobs. Use checksum-based validation versus the current canonical aggregate job. Once validated, flip Console dashboard data source to the new views during a low-traffic window and keep fallback route to raw-event queries for 48 hours.
backfill_plan: Backfill strategy: 30-day historical backfill in two phases: Phase A (first 7 days) for correctness validation; Phase B (remaining 23 days) for full populate. Rate limit via job controller to keep warehouse slot usage under 60% of peak. Estimated S3 read: ~1.2TB, compute hours: ~18 core-hours per partition. Progress tracked in backfill-run docs and PRs.
risks: R1: Identity churn (workspace migrations / user unlinks) causing session splits — mitigated by identity mapping table and best-effort merges during compaction.
R2: Hive/Metastore schema evolution conflict during concurrent MERGE — mitigate by coordinated schema rollout and migration lock job.
R3: Small-file explosion if CDC applies many tiny upserts — mitigate via batching and periodic compaction run with thresholds.
R4: Dashboard regressions if p99 latency computed differently — mitigate with shadow queries and histogram parity checks before cutover.
